qs.q: A 30‑year‑old man with severe onychomycosis is prescribed terbinafine; after 4 weeks he complains of taste alteration. Which enzyme inhibition is most directly linked to this side effect?
o: Inhibition of fungal squalene epoxidase reducing sterols
Stimulation of human CYP2C9 causing mucosal changes
Activation of human CYP1A2 leading to taste buildup
Inhibition of human CYP3A4 altering salivary enzymes
Blockade of human cytochrome P450 2D6 affecting taste
qs.e: Terbinafine inhibits CYP2D6, which can affect taste perception.

qs.q: A medical student is reviewing drug interactions for antihistamines. Which class of drugs is noted to interact with certain first-generation antihistamines via enzyme inhibition?
qs.e: First-generation antihistamines interact with enzyme inhibitors such as macrolides, antifungals, and calcium antagonists. Beta-blockers do not share this specific metabolic drug interaction profile in the context of antihistamines.
